title: Structs
summary: Named fields, instantiated with braces; update syntax ..other copies the rest.
lecture: A struct names a shape: `struct User { name: String }`. Each field has a type; you build a value by naming every field: `User { name: String::from("Ferris") }`. Missing fields are error E0063 - there are no partially built structs.
Struct update syntax fills in the tail from another value: `Order { count: 2, ..base }` takes every remaining field from `base`. It must come last in the braces.
Methods live in an `impl` block. A method that only reads takes `&self`; one that consumes the value takes `self`. Calling a `self` method twice on the same value is E0382 - the first call moved it.

example.caption: &self lets you call cost() as many times as you like.
